observations: Photo 0 shows a dry pressing iron (no visible water tank).
The iron body is white/gray with a soleplate facing down; there are visible stains/scuffs on the soleplate area.
The power cord and plug are visible; the plug end looks worn/dirty and the cord shows age/usage.
No brand/model label is readable in the photo.

claims.claim: A used dry pressing iron that is still working is available for sale.
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows the iron and cord, but there is no power-on test, no indicator, and no readable brand/model or condition proof.

risks.risk: Not actually working (heater/thermostat may be faulty).
risks.proof: A short video of the iron plugged in and heating (e.g., temperature/steam-less heat-up test on a cloth) with the plug/cable shown.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working / needs repair.

risks.risk: Damaged or unsafe power cord/plug (could cause intermittent power or short).
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the plug pins and the full cord length (especially near the plug and where it enters the iron), plus a power-on test.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as requiring cord/plug replacement or electrical risk.

risks.risk: Soleplate wear or damage affecting ironing performance (staining, uneven heating, scratches).
risks.proof: Clear close-up of the soleplate surface (straight-on) showing scratches/burn marks, plus a test ironing pass on fabric.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as cosmetically worn and potentially less effective.

proof_requests: Send a video showing the iron plugged in and heating properly (no sparks, stable power).
Send close-up photos of the plug and cord ends (especially where the cord meets the iron).
Send a clear close-up of the soleplate surface and a quick ironing test on a piece of cloth.
response.reason: The photo confirms it’s a used dry pressing iron, but the key claim that it is still working is not verifiable remotely without a power-on/heating test and cord safety check.
